Screens:
Tournaments · every screen an organizer works in · a deep dive

The tournament admin, walked end to end, on a phone and at a desk

On 28 September every tournament screen took the coaches portal's look, Warm and Dark, with the same layouts and words. This walk reads the screens as they now stand, in the order an organizer meets them: create, set up, teams, the schedule, game day, the volunteers, after the event. For each station you get what's on the screen and its numbers, how it feels to use, and a shape question. Stage 1 (game day) is drawn at true size on its own tab. You read both against the product and tell me what to change or add.

How to read this

  • Thirteen stations. Each has as built (captures and browser-measured numbers), my read (what works, what gets in the way, what I'd change) and one or two shape questions with Keep · Reshape · Not yet and a notes box.
  • Then standing back (nine rules across the stations), the stages, the asks (A1–A10, a checkbox per option) and your rulings to paste back.
  • Every red flag, green chip and NEW / RESTYLED / UNCHANGED tag opens its explanation when clicked. A a guess tag marks a claim that rests on how a director will behave, not on a measurement.
  • The Warm / Dark switch at the top turns every drawn screen and, where one exists, every capture.

Where I walked

  • A read-only browser probe at 390×844 and 360×780 (phones, touch), 768×1024 (tablet, touch) and 1440×900 (desk), Warm and Dark. It opened windows and menus and closed them; every write was refused.
  • Numbers come from the browser's own geometry. Captures are the browser's own pictures of the same pages.
  • The June persona walks were re-checked against today's code. A June row counts as open only where the code still does it: of 76 organizer rows, 26 are fixed, 9 partly, 6 changed and 32 open; of 23 volunteer rows, 14 fixed, 4 partly, 1 changed, 3 open.
WhereWhat

It is the only dev tournament with games, and its weekend is past: 2 games final, 2 waiting to be finalized, 6 that never got a score, 1 cancelled.

1

Creating a tournament: two wizards, and only the first asks about diamonds

An organizer creates their event, then next year's.

New tournament · the rail's + or Tournaments → New Tournament · and the first-run setup a new organization sees once
On the screen, as built

From the Tournaments list, New Tournament opens a window. An organization that has run an event first sees Start blank or Reuse a previous tournament setup; then five steps: the tournament (name, dates, style, address), divisions, a welcome message, venues, review. Nothing saves until Save setup on the last step, which is the house rule for creating. At a desk a live phone-shaped preview of the public page sits beside it.

The first-run setup a brand-new organization walks through asks, for each park, how many fields or diamonds it has, and creates Diamond 1…N so the schedule has lanes. That was June's J1-028 fix. The New Tournament wizard, the path every event after the first takes, asks for a street address only. Neither asks for fees; that was ruled optional on 16 June, and the launch check agrees.

create, blank: 5 clicks (Next ×4, Save)+1 when past events exist (Start blank)phone window 366×384 at the pre-stepPlus notice: no styling at all

How it feels to use: my read

What works

  • Create asks, and nothing is half-made. One save at the end, a preview at a desk, every step skippable.
  • Reuse is offered at the moment it matters, when an organizer starts their second event.

What gets in the way

  • The second event is set up worse than the first. A three-diamond park created here becomes one scheduling lane until the organizer finds Venues & facilities.
  • A Tournament-plan organizer's "reuse needs Plus" line has no box, colour or edge: its styling is defined nowhere, so it reads as stray text.

What I'd change

  • One set of creation questions for both wizards, diamonds included (Stage 5). The notice's styling is a defect for the list below (A8).
Q 1.1 · Stage 5

Should the New Tournament wizard ask the first-run setup's question about fields and diamonds?

It is the one creation answer that changes the schedule the generator builds.

Recommendation: Reshape, in Stage 5: both wizards ask the same questions.

What rides on it: the Venues screen stays where facilities are managed; the wizard only seeds Diamond 1…N, as the first-run setup already does.

2

Event settings: seven closed cards that fit one phone screen, and one control that spills

An organizer sets fees, contacts, rosters and the schedule's rules.

Setup → Event settings · autosaves, a "Saved" that fades
On the screen, as built

Seven cards, each closed and each carrying a one-line summary (Fees & Payments · Per division, Schedule Rules · Round robin + playoffs · 90m games). A link from the launch checklist opens the right card. Everything autosaves; only the public address and the organization address ask first, because they change something public. June's "wall of closed doors" (J1-029) is fixed on both counts.

7 cards fit one phone screen (to 602px)fee buttons 38px tall (the admin's ruled height)Fee model: +15px past the edge at 360

How it feels to use: my read

What works

  • The best setup screen in the tournament product: scannable closed, deep-linkable, autosaving. The other setup screens should learn from it (F30).

What gets in the way

  • The Fee model's four buttons don't fit a small phone.

What I'd change

  • Keep the screen; the Fee model becomes a dropdown on a phone (form selects are dropdowns), in Stage 5.
Q 2.1 · Stage 5

Is Event settings the pattern the other setup screens follow?

Closed cards with summaries, autosave, a link that opens the right card. Divisions, Venues, Rules and Public site each save a different way today.

Recommendation: Keep this screen as it is, and make it the model in Stage 5.

What rides on it: Rules' leave-guard and three-way leave dialog, and Public site's single bottom Save, both go.

3

Divisions, venues and rules: a sold-out division painted as a failure

An organizer adds divisions, parks with their diamonds, and the rulebook.

Setup → Divisions · Venues & facilities · Rules & resources
On the screen, as built

Divisions is a card per division with a capacity gauge; a full one reads FULL in the danger colour, and every card carries twin Edit and Delete icons whether or not games are scheduled. Adding one is two clicks (Add, Save). Venues & facilities is where a park's diamonds are managed; it has no help link. Rules & resources saves each section on its own, adds a point instantly, and guards against leaving with a three-way dialog.

add a division: 2 clicksEdit / Delete: 35×25 each, side by sideRules' Browse samples / Add section: 36×26Venues' export: 32×32

How it feels to use: my read

What works

  • Deleting is careful: a division with games asks again with real counts; a venue with a played game can only be renamed.

What gets in the way

  • Full is good news, drawn as bad news, and Delete sits beside Edit at equal weight on a live event's cards; errors come in the browser's own alert box.
  • Four setup screens, four ways of saving: an organizer can't learn one "did that stick?".

What I'd change

  • Stage 5: full reads as good news; Delete moves into the division's own editor (delete is never a row action); one save model, Event settings'.
Q 3.1 · Stage 5

Should the setup screens move to one save model, autosave with the fading "Saved", and put Delete inside each record's editor?

Recommendation: Reshape, in Stage 5. a guess on how much Rules' leave-guard is used; a first director would tell us.

What rides on it: the "edit autosaves, create asks" rule already says it; adding a division or a venue still asks.

Public site: the editor never shows the page it edits

An organizer chooses the public pages and, on Plus, the logo, theme and banner.

Setup → Public site
On the screen, as built

Public Pages (which pages appear) is open; then six branding cards, each locked on the Tournament plan; then one Save at the foot. No link on the page opens the public site or its preview; the theme's "preview" is a drawn card, not the page. The dashboard's "what everyone else sees" panel is the only door to the preview, and it shows only while the event is a draft.

Save at 1,255px on a phone (1.8 screens)links to the site: 0Tournament plan: 6 locked cards

How it feels to use: my read

What gets in the way

  • Change the banner, and the page gives no way to see it.

What I'd change

  • Stage 5: a "See your public site" door in the header (the preview while a draft, the live page after), and the save that follows the rule.
Q 4.1 · Stage 5

Should Public site carry a door to the public page it edits?

Recommendation: Reshape, in Stage 5. The door is one link; the preview itself stays the public page's own (out of scope).

6

Teams: on a phone, no team is on the first screen, and the pools view pushes buttons off it

On registration days an organizer accepts, waitlists and places teams.

Operations → Teams · the flat list, the pools (slot) board, registration health, payments
On the screen, as built

A division with pools opens on the slot board. Above it, in order: the page header, the toolbar (division, the pools tools), Registration health (closed), the capacity line, and Payments, which opens by default on a phone and takes 287px. On a phone each slot row keeps two fixed-width columns (130px + 160px), so its status badges and its own open button end past the right edge, where the card hides them. "Accepted" is green in the flat list, grey on the slot board and lime on the phone's row marker.

first team at 864px on a phone (the screen ends at 844)row button +152 to +179px off the edge at 390 · +182 to +209px at 360row buttons 24×24first team at 699px at 1440

How it feels to use: my read

What works

  • Accepting into a pool claims the slot (June's vanishing team is fixed), payments read in one place, and the waitlist promotes.

What gets in the way

  • The list the screen exists for starts below the first phone screen.
  • A team's own button can't be reached on a phone.
  • One status, three colours, and glyphs instead of words on a phone.

What I'd change

  • Stage 2: the first team on screen one (payments and health as closed rows), a row that fits the phone and opens the team, one colour per status and words on a phone. The unreachable button is a defect now (A8).
  • Drawn on the Stage 2 tab (30 Sep), with what the re-walk added: a team waiting for a decision is not on the pool board at all (F41).
Q 6.1 · Stage 2

Should Teams open with the teams first, and the money and health readouts as closed rows above them?

Recommendation: Reshape, in Stage 2.

What rides on it: the demo tour's registration-health anchor stays on the health row (the demo force-opens it); Payments is the Club Stage 7 seam (fees to the club ledger), drawn as today's behaviour.

Communications: an upsell for a feature that isn't there

An organizer messages every team, or posts to the public news.

Operations → Communications · site posts, emails, push
On the screen, as built

One composer for the site, email and push, five quick templates, and per-recipient delivery. Under it a hint says Plus unlocks targeting, shown on every plan; the composer has no audience picker on any plan (June's J1-070, still open).

message every team: New Message → write → Sendfilter tabs 28px tall

How it feels to use: my read

What gets in the way

  • A Plus organizer is told to upgrade for targeting they can't find.

What I'd change

  • Stage 2: build targeting for Plus, or take the hint down. Which one is a packaging call for /strategy, not a drawing.
  • Drawn on the Stage 2 tab (30 Sep), with what the re-walk added: the email reaches every registered team while it says “all accepted teams” (F42).
8

The schedule: it opens on an empty list once a division has played

An organizer builds the round robin and the bracket, publishes, and moves games when the day slips.

Operations → Schedule · list · timeline · bracket · health · Tools (generator, bracket, rain delay) · Publish
On the screen, as built

It opens on the first division's round robin showing unplayed games only. U11 Girls' two games are played, so at both widths the page opens on "No games match your filters. Clear filters". Publish covers both stages (June's J1-076 is fixed). On a phone the timeline opens on today with a "now" line. The bracket shows names, time and field, and never a score or a winner. The generator is "Round-Robin Generator" on every door and "Schedule Generator" inside. The rain-delay tool is good: push a day's games by 30 minutes to 2 hours, cancel one, apply once. It lives behind Tools, on Tournament Plus.

opens on "No games match your filters" at 390 and 1440rain delay: board → Schedule → Tools → Rain delay = 3 tapsTools button 48×34 on a phone

How it feels to use: my read

What works

  • The rain-delay tool, the timeline's "today", the bracket's order checks. June's biggest schedule gaps are closed.

What gets in the way

  • Mid-weekend, the schedule opens empty. a guess that an organizer wants the day, played or not.
  • The bracket can't tell you who won. One tool, two names ; a dragged game moves with no undo ; the coin toss is recorded on the public preview only .

What I'd change

  • Stage 3. The rain-delay tool gets a door from the game-day board in Stage 1 (G8), where Storm Mode will later live.
Q 8.1 · Stage 3

Should the schedule open on the whole day, played games included?

Recommendation: Reshape, in Stage 3 (today's filters stay one tap away).

What rides on it: the demo tour's schedule-health anchor stays on the health panel.

9

The game-day board: the right games, in the wrong order, with doors that lose the game

On the weekend an organizer opens the dashboard to see what needs them.

Operations → Dashboard on game day · polls every 30 s
On the screen, as built

Pinned at the top, the event header: org, dates, the name, one status chip, the public-site pill (113px on a phone at rest, 70px once scrolled). Under it the dashboard draws its own header: the org, the name again, then ACTIVE and LIVE, while the event header's chip says OPEN or LIVE (two rules decide the phase) and the guidance card says "It's game day". Then the board: Now playing (which also holds scores waiting to be finalized), Up next, Needs a score (times, no day), games progress, check-in, schedule health, by division. The line that says the event can be marked complete is last. Every row, and every "Enter scores →", opens Results with no game named.

board 2,502px at 390 (3.0 screens) · 1,357px at 1440first game at 347px on a phone"Enter scores →" 77×17, "Review ->" 49×17board → score box: 5 tapsnext-step line at 2,187px

How it feels to use: my read

What works

  • The board knows the day. Live, overdue, next, a champion the moment a final is final, a 30-second refresh. The data is right; the shape isn't.

What gets in the way

  • The event is named twice and its status four times.
  • A game on the board opens a list you search again.
  • Scores waiting for the organizer are filed under "Now playing", and overdue games have no day.
  • Three phone screens, the next step at the bottom, and 17px doors.

What I'd change

  • Stage 1, drawn on its own tab: one event identity (G1), the board in the order of the day (G2), every game opening that game (G3), a place for Storm Mode (G8).
Q 9.1 · Stage 1

Should the game-day board open on what needs the organizer: scores to finalize, then games that need a score, then what's live and next?

Today's order leads with "Now playing". a guess that a director at a diamond is looking for the work before the scoreboard; a first director would confirm it. Waiting would cost little, but Stage 1 redraws the board anyway.

Recommendation: Reshape, as drawn in Stage 1 (G2). Customize stays, so a director who wants the scoreboard first can drag it there.

What rides on it: the demo tour's now-playing anchor stays on the Playing-now list and still appears only while a demo game is live.

10

Results: it opens on one division, and its most-used controls are 22px

An organizer enters, checks and finalizes scores.

Operations → Results · the game list in scoring mode · fetches once
On the screen, as built

The page opens on the first division with every status showing: on the test event, U11 Girls' two games out of ten. The six that need a score are in the other divisions. Each game is a stacked row (the two teams and their scores, kept on §245). The pencil opens the score editor in place; a waiting score carries Finalize, a word at a desk and a bare tick on a phone. On a phone the waiting count is a coloured dot and a number with no word, hidden from screen readers. A tie wears the "didn't win" ink on both sides. The page never refreshes itself, and its empty state promises "no refresh needed".

games visible on open: 2 of 10pencil 22×22 · Finalize tick 35×25 (phone)first game at 483px on a phonerow height 83px, and tapping it does nothing

How it feels to use: my read

What works

  • A score is entered in place, with −/+ steppers, and a waiting score finalizes in one tap. Results can already open one named game (the notifications use it).

What gets in the way

  • Most of the day is behind the division menu.
  • The two controls used most are the smallest.
  • It doesn't refresh itself, a tie looks unplayed, and the same state has four names.

What I'd change

  • Stage 1: open on "needs you" across every division (G4, A10), the whole row as the door, a worded Finalize, Tie said, one word per state (G5), and a page that stays current (G6).
Q 10.1 · Stage 1

Should Results open on the games that need the organizer, in every division?

Recommendation: Reshape, as drawn (G4). "Show all games" and the division menu stay one tap away.

What rides on it: the export still exports everything; a notification's link still opens its one game.

11

Check-in: two person icons side by side on every row

As teams arrive, the organizer or a gate volunteer checks them in and takes the balance.

Operations → Check-in · the same board the gate volunteer uses · fetches once · and Staff kit, Chat
On the screen, as built

Three gauges (checked in, no-shows, unpaid), a search, a division menu, a four-way filter, then the teams by division. On a phone each row ends in No-show and Check in, both icons of a person, both without words. Tapping the row opens the team's sheet, which is right: payment, roster, and No-show a third beside Check in two thirds, 48px. Neither this page nor the gate's copy of it refreshes, so two volunteers never see each other's check-ins. Staff kit (QR codes and links for the volunteers) needs nothing. Chat has no page title.

row: No-show 38×38 + Check in 34×38, both icon-onlyfilters 24px tallfirst team at 490pxthe sheet: 48px buttons ✓

How it feels to use: my read

What works

  • The team sheet, Undo on every arrival, reversible payment, a roster edit that no longer overwrites the coach's. June's gate hazards are fixed.

What gets in the way

  • One mis-tap marks a team a no-show.
  • The counts don't filter, and the filters are 24px. The same board is the gate's , so every change here reaches the volunteers.
  • Chat has no page title .

What I'd change

  • Stage 1 (G7): one worded Check in per row, No-show inside the sheet, the counts become the filter.
Q 11.1 · Stage 1

Should No-show leave the row and live only in the team's sheet?

It is the rarer action and the one that is hard to see you got wrong. The sheet already asks it at the right weight.

Recommendation: Reshape, as drawn (G7). Marking a no-show becomes 2 taps (the row, then No-show); checking in stays 1.

What rides on it: the gate volunteer's board changes the same way (walked on §245 W5).

The scorekeeper and the gate: the strongest screens in the tournament product

A parent handed a phone at the scoring table or the gate does one job, fast.

/scorekeeper and /check-in · fixed Warm (R3) · the plus-official account
On the screen, as built

Since June the volunteer screens were rebuilt: sign-out works, an expired session recovers, the soonest game carries a lime "Up next", the score is one large box (steppers were tried and removed: they left 29px for the numeral), the review note is coloured and iconed, payment reverses, and a gate roster edit no longer overwrites the coach's. 14 of June's 23 findings are fixed. Four items remain.

score box 72px tallCancel / Submit 42pxinstall banner can cover the filter and tab bars

How it feels to use: my read

What gets in the way

  • The install banner sits on the shell's own bars; buttons at 42px; the Review filter doesn't signal waiting scores; a staff member lands on the full dashboard.

What I'd change

  • Stage 6, phone only. The gate's board changes in Stage 1 with the organizer's (F13).
  • Drawn on the Stage 6 tab (7 Oct), re-measured: the banner covers the buckets and an open score sheet on an iPhone (F58), the bars are see-through (F59), a gate volunteer lands on the scorekeeper (F62), and the Staff kit prints the admin (F65).
13

After the event: a restore that isn't there, and "run it back" in two places

An organizer closes the event, shares the results, archives it and sets up next year.

Post-event summary · Past tournaments (Archives) · Data tools · the Tournaments list
On the screen, as built

The dashboard's archive confirm says "You can restore it later from Past Tournaments". Past tournaments offers Seal and View only; restoring is the Tournaments list's status menu, which the plan's slot limit can block. It never says the public site goes offline, which the Tournaments list's own confirm does. Summary on a phone is one figure per card ("0 champions detected"); Share links the standings but not the champions page; "What's next" with the reuse button is closed, 1,713px down. Reuse also lives on the Tournaments list, as a different flow. The completed dashboard offers neither.

archive confirm: a restore that doesn't existreuse: 2 flows, 1 tap (list) vs 3 (Summary)Summary cards 143px each on a phone

How it feels to use: my read

What gets in the way

  • A destructive action's confirm promises something the product doesn't do.
  • Two reuse flows, and none where the event ends.

What I'd change

  • Stage 4: the finished board celebrates and offers "Run it back"; one reuse flow. The archive sentence and the leader sort are defects now (A8).
  • Drawn on the Stage 4 tab (5 Oct), with what the re-walk added: no door to the Tournaments list from inside an event (F48), and on the free plan next year's event costs this year's public site (F49).
Q 13.1 · Stage 4

Should there be one "Run it back" flow, offered on the finished event's board?

Recommendation: Reshape, in Stage 4: the wizard's reuse step is the one flow; Summary and the finished board open it.

Standing back: nine rules across the walk

Each rule is what the stations have in common. The stages apply them one area at a time.

  1. 1
    Name the event once. The pinned event header is the event's identity; a page names only itself.16 of 23 screens repeat the name directly under the header as their eyebrow; the dashboard repeats it as its title, with its status (F01).
  2. 2
    One status, one rule, one word. A phase and a game state are computed once and spelled once.Two rules for "game day" (F01); four names for a waiting score (F10); three colours for Accepted (F17).
  3. 3
    A row opens its own record. A game opens that game, never a list you search again.The board's rows (F02); Results' 83px rows that do nothing (F07); Teams' unreachable row button (F16).
  4. 4
    Open on what needs you. A working screen opens on the work, in every division.Results on one division (F06); the schedule empty mid-weekend (F19); Teams' list below the fold (F15).
  5. 5
    Game day stays current by itself.The board refreshes every 30 s; Results and Check-in never do (F08).
  6. 6
    The control used most is the biggest. The daily job gets the row or a worded 44px button; the rare or destructive one moves into the record's sheet.22px pencil, 25px Finalize, 17px board doors, twin person icons (F05, F07, F11).
  7. 7
    A phone row fits the phone.Pools rows +152–209px (F16); Fee model +15px at 360 (F27).
  8. 8
    One way to do one thing.Two creation wizards (F25), two reuse flows (F33), two archive sentences (F32), one generator with two names (F21), four save models (F30).
  9. 9
    Say the true thing.A restore that isn't there (F32); "no refresh needed" (F08); "Plus unlocks targeting" (F18).

The stages

Proposed from what the walk found, not from the four job groups the foundation named. Each is drawn, ruled, built after Part B's cleanup has passed over its screens, and walked. Only Stage 1 is drawn today.

Why game day first. It is the weekend a director is judged on, the one time the product is used from a phone under time pressure, and where June's walk and the foundation both found the most friction: five taps to a score, most of the day hidden on Results, a 22px pencil, screens that don't refresh, twin icons at the gate. Teams has the worst single number (no team on the first screen), but registration happens over weeks, at a desk.

The asks

One checkbox per option. The recommendation is the first option. The paste-back below collects every ticked box and note.

Your rulings, to paste back

This gathers your Keep / Reshape / Not yet answers, the asks you ticked, your Stage 1 rulings and every note, from both tabs. It stays in this browser until you paste it back to me.

Game day: the board opens on what needs you, and every game opens that game

Three screens an organizer lives in on the weekend: the board, Results and Check-in. Before is today's screen, captured on the test event at 390 and 1440 (scroll inside a phone frame, just as on a phone). After is drawn in Warm, and a Dark copy follows each one. Every tag and chip opens its note; the striped square beside each phone is 44px, the size of a fingertip target. This version is redrawn against the portal's written formatting rules; the formatting check at the foot of this tab lists every fix, and A11 draws both answers to the one question the rules leave open.

G1 · One event, named once, with one status

The pinned event header already names the event and its dates, and carries the switcher. Today the pages under it name the event again, and the dashboard draws a second header with two more status tags. After: the header carries one chip from one rule (the board's own: the event's dates, or its first game having started, until it is marked complete), on the dates line, so a phone header is two lines. Pages name only themselves. The dashboard keeps its page title, "Dashboard", the way every portal screen keeps its title band (the portal's own home kept "Overview" after a version without one was rejected on sight). It carries no status tags, because the header's chip is the status.

G2 · G3 · The board opens on what needs you, and a game opens that game

Four lists in the order of the organizer's day, each hidden when empty: To finalize (scores submitted, waiting for the organizer: today they sit under "Now playing"), Needs a score (overdue, with the day when it isn't today), Playing now (live only), Up next. G4 · Your ruling · also answers A10

G5 · One word per game state

The same four states read ten ways across the screens an organizer and a scorekeeper use in the same hour. The one-spelling rule is a product rule: a word a customer reads has one spelling everywhere. Pending Review stays as the product spells it (kept on §245). The rest align to it. The words are tagged for /marketing.

StateThe board todayResults todaySchedule tag todayScorekeeper todayEverywhere, proposed Copy
No score yet, time passedNEEDS SCOREUnscoredScheduled (+ Overdue)To ScoreNeeds a score
Submitted, waiting for the organizerIN REVIEWReviewingPending ReviewReviewPending Review (a list heading on the board reads "To finalize")
Final(counted)Completed✓ FinalFinalFinal
Forfeit(counted)Forfeit⚑ Forfeit—Forfeit
Level score—(no word)(no word)—Tie

The phone's waiting count on Results gets its words ("2 Pending Review"), not a bare dot and number hidden from screen readers.

G5 · Your ruling · also answers A7

G6 · Game day stays current by itself

The board refreshes every 30 seconds while it is on screen. Results and Check-in fetch once, so a scorekeeper's submission or a second gate volunteer's check-in appears only after a reload, while Results' empty state promises "no refresh needed". After: both refresh the same way the board does, and the false line goes. Nothing new is drawn: no "live" badge and no "updated" clock; the page simply stays right. An open score editor is never refreshed out from under the organizer.

G6 · Your ruling · also answers A9

G7 · Check-in: the word on the button used most, and the counts become the filter

On a phone each row carries one worded Check in (44px) and ends in its chevron, which opens the team's sheet. No-show moves into that sheet, which already asks it at the right weight (a third, beside Check in at two thirds, both 48px). A checked-in row shows its time and a worded Undo. The counts become the filter, as the gate volunteer's own bar: four equal buttons, All, Not arrived, Checked in and No-show, the count on top, All chosen when the page opens (as today). Who still owes is a count under it, not a button: payment is a different question from arrival, and a row already says "Owes $475". The 24px filter goes. The gate volunteer's board is this board, so it changes the same way. Where the worded button sits on a phone is ask A11; this frame shows option 1, one frame with the button in the row.

G7 · Your ruling

A11 · A worded button on a phone: in the row, or a row of its own

The portal has two forms for a list on a phone. When a list's rows fit a phone, it stays one frame, the same as at a desk (the Overview board, the Schedule's list), and a row's one worded action sits in the row beside its chevron, as the 2026-09-04 ruling allows when the action fires on most rows. When the rows do not fit, the list breaks into row-cards, and there the table standard's K-09 puts a worded action on a full-width 44px row across the card's foot. Check-in's and Results' rows fit, so Option 1 is the portal's own form, not an exception. Option 2 draws the row-card form anyway, for the bigger target. Both frames show the same teams on the same screen, so count the teams you can see above the tab bar. (Before your question about the gaps, this section drew Option 1 as separate cards and called it an exception; that was my misreading of the standard.)

The scores get the card's width; the button gets its own row.

My recommendation is Option 1, and now more firmly. It is the portal's own form for a list that fits a phone, so the tournament screens would match the coaches portal instead of carrying an exception. Check-in is also a queue at a gate: the volunteer scans for the team in front of them, and every team on screen one is a scroll saved at the busiest minute of the day. The risk is the neighbouring tap: the button is 44px and the row's tap is the rest of the row, so the two targets touch but never overlap. Option 2 removes that risk, and the gate sees 4 teams on screen one instead of 6. At a desk the question doesn't arise: both options draw the desk table above.

G8 · A place for Storm Mode and the Big Board, and the plan lock with words

Storm Mode ("declare a delay") and the Big Board ("show on a screen") are their own projects, and nothing of either is drawn here. The board gains one door, Running late?, to today's rain-delay tool (on the schedule's Tools menu today, three taps from the board), drawn as the kit's door card because it opens another tool. That door is where Storm Mode will land. A reserved place beside "Public site" in the desk header marks where the Big Board's door would go. For a Tournament-plan organizer the rain-delay tool is Plus: the door stays, with the lock and the plan's name (A6); today's padlocks carry none.

G8 · Your ruling · also answers A4 and A6

The formatting check, and what this redraw changed

On 29 September Stage 1's drawings were checked against the portal's written rules: the table and list standard, its exception register, the kit, the page-header and section rules, the type ladder, and your nine formatting rulings of 28 September. The drawn sizes were read in a browser, and a second reviewer checked independently. It found fifteen departures, and your question about the gaps on the phone board found a sixteenth that both reviewers missed. Every one is fixed in this version; the two questions the rules leave open are yours to rule, and one of them already is.

#What was drawnThe ruleIn this version
1The dashboard had no page title (the event header was its title)The title band survives on every portal screen; the no-title home was rejected on sight"Dashboard", title face, 20px, no tags
2"2 to finalize" said four times on the phone boardA status is said onceThe count is the list heading's; the top note says only the step the lists can't (the strip is the frame's, F39)
3Rows with a worded button had no chevronA chevron closes every row; one worded action may sit beside itEvery row ends in its chevron
4The overdue day in amber; "Paid" in greenStatus colour lives in a chip, or on a figure that is bad newsThe day in the caption's ink; "Paid" plain; "Owes" stays amber (money owed). The winner's green score is today's, kept: a question for the register
5Desk rows laid out as columns with no heading rowA table always has its heading row; a row list has no data columnsThe board and Results are row lists; Check-in is a table with its headings
6Two filter shapes (pills on Results, count tiles on Check-in)One shape: the kit's filter pill with its countResults: the pill, 12px, 44px on a phone, 38px at a desk. Check-in: the gate volunteer's own four-button bar, because it is the gate's board (your ruling, 29 September: All first and the default; payment a count, not a button)
7Schedule health's right chevron on a row that expandsA right chevron opens, a down chevron expands (ruling 3)The down chevron
8Nine text sizes off the ladderEight steps: 10 · 11 · 12 · 14 · 16 · 20 · 24 · 32Desk title 20; figures 24; row titles 14; captions 12; phone event name 16
9The event header's eyebrow lighter and tighter than the real oneThe kit's eyebrow: 11px mono, bold, trackedThe kit's eyebrow, at both widths
10The score editor's corners matched nothing (12px)A part keeps its family's radiusIt opens in its row's place inside the list's frame, with no corners of its own
11A band's count beside the label in one place, right-aligned in anotherOne band-row shapeThe label, then its count, everywhere
12Desk row buttons 36pxThe admin's own control height, 38px (K-18)38px
13"Running late?" as a record rowA door to another place is the kit's door cardThe door card: a lift, the arrow in its eyebrow
14Dates as "Fri Jun 12"The product's own date form"Fri, Jun 12"

T5 · One colour per status, and words, not letters

Measured on 30 September in both themes: Accepted is green in the desk list, warm grey on the pool board, and an olive letter “A” on a phone (lime on navy in Dark). On a phone the status is a 9px letter (P, A, W, R) and the payment is one or two “$” glyphs 7px wide, coloured. After: the status is said once, by the band a team sits under (To review · a pool · Accepted · Waitlist · Needs a spot). Where a status needs a chip — the team's record, or a row whose status differs from its band — it takes the club's own tone map (Club Tier's tryouts: pending amber, accepted green, waitlisted and declined neutral), so the admin has one. Payment is Check-in's words: “Owes $475” amber, “Paid” plain.

T6 · A division without pool slots, and an Exhibition event

U15 Open has no pools. Today its phone list is a stack of separate cards (a letter and “$” glyphs on each), under a “POOLS” view strip and a note that pools aren't turned on, with a Randomize that can only say it needs two pools. Build-time calls (on the walk)

  • The save word (“Saved”, and why a save is held) sits in the record’s head beside the name — the kit form window’s status slot; the drawing did not say where.
  • Accept, Reject, Delete and the rest ask in the kit’s question window, on top of the record.
  • An open spot is a row of its own on the pool board (“Red Team 3 · Open spot”), so Swap can move a team into it.
  • An email’s delivery sits inside its record, with “See who it reached” opening the list in place.
  • The reminder window moved onto the kit’s form window with no change of words.
  • The Teams choice “Every registered team” reads All except rejected (/marketing): a rejected team is never emailed.
  • On a phone the view settings are a sheet (Group by · Registration status · Payment status).

The review, before the commit

/review (high-risk tier, five lenses) found and fixed: the record could send two saves at once while you stepped between teams, and a Mark paid could be undone by a figure typed a moment before it — the record now saves one change at a time and every action saves first; half an email was saved as the team’s sign-in address — now held, with words waiting on /marketing; a slow first read could flip the chosen division, and every division change re-read the whole event; an older spot read could paint over a newer one; a team on a spot in a pool deleted a moment ago vanished; Communications blanked after every send; a template counted as unsaved; push no longer said it posts to the site; the locked banner lost Upgrade. Reported, not fixed: a single waitlisted team accepted by hand keeps its old waitlist number on the server; Teams’ shared export menu is 32px on a phone (all 47 screens); two quick actions on different rows share one busy mark (as today).

Teams toolbar · a Stage 2 follow-up from the §252 walk · true size · open this tab on your phone · drawn, ruled and built 1 October 2026

One toolbar in every division, with the rarer tools in one menu

Your question from the walk: “why are the action buttons so different between these, we lose filtering and search when we have pools? … should there be a ‘tools’ button?” Today Teams draws two different toolbars. A division whose pools have numbered spots (U11 Girls: Red Team 1, 2, 3) gets Select many, Swap and Randomize, and no search or filters. A division without spots (U15 Open) gets search, filters and Select many. The Stage 2 tab drew it that way and you ruled it as drawn on 30 September (T1 draws the board’s line as its three tools; T6 draws the list’s line with search and the view sheet), but neither drawing said a board loses search and filters, so the question was never put to you. The reason underneath: a board draws every spot, including the empty ones, so a filter had nothing to hide.

Ruled 1 October: A, as drawn, without the note under a search (“I agree with A but we don’t need this explanation after searching, users know how to clear search and what searching does to filtering”). That carries TB2 (a list), TB3 (Registration questions into Tools) and TB4 (one Filter menu and one Tools menu at a desk) as drawn. Built the same day; the search frame below is redrawn without the note. Two build-time calls, for you to overrule: a filter is no longer remembered between visits (a filter left on would open a pool board as a list with nothing saying why; the division and the grouping are still remembered), and a payment filter lists only accepted teams (before, Unpaid also listed a team still to review or on the waitlist, whose Payment reads “—”).

Recommended (option A): the same four things in every division, at every width: the division, Search, Filter, and Tools. Tools holds Select many, Swap, Randomize and Registration questions; a tool that does not apply to the division is absent from the menu. A search or a filter on a pool board shows the matching teams as a list, and clearing it brings the board back; the dashboard’s “to review” link already does exactly this. Two other arrangements are drawn so you can compare, with the division box’s width measured at 360 and 390. Every NEW / RESTYLED / UNCHANGED tag opens its note; the striped square beside each phone is 44px.

The formatting check, run before you saw it

  • Tap targets. Every phone control is 44px; the sheet’s rows are 48px. Desk controls take the admin’s 38px (K-18).
  • One lime per screen: Add team, unchanged.
  • The phone’s panel is a sheet, the portal’s form for every phone panel (2026-09-22), and the ⋯ square is the practice plan’s toolbar form (E1). ⋯ is used only as a toolbar’s second row, never on a list row (the table standard).
  • What does not apply is absent, not disabled (the Exhibition ruling): Swap only with numbered spots, Randomize only with two pools, Registration questions only on Tournament Plus.
  • The waiting mark on the division box is the rail’s amber (ruled today).
  • Words: today’s labels are kept (Select many, Swap, Randomize, Registration questions, Filter). “Tools” and its group names (Teams, Pools, Setup) are new, for /marketing; the match note and its Clear were dropped by the ruling.
  • Not asked here: Export. It stays in the title band, as on every admin screen. The coaches portal puts an export in the toolbar above what it exports (house rule 2, 2026-08-23); moving the admin’s is one decision for every admin screen with an export, not this one, and is left for you to raise.

The formatting check, run before you saw it

Stage 1's sixteen departures (plan §11) are the checklist, with the table standard's §3.5–3.7 and §3.10, the exception register and every ruling since Stage 2 (30 September – 5 October). Each row is what the drawing does and the rule it answers to. Where the rules leave something open, it is an ask above, not a silent pick.

#The checkThe ruleThis drawing
1A screen without its title bandEvery screen keeps its title bandDashboard, Summary, Past tournaments, Tournaments: title face 20px, icons on the line on a phone
2A fact said more than onceA status is said once"Complete" once (the event header's chip); one door to Summary on the board (today three, two lime) — the strip above the bar gives way where the page carries the same door; the champion once per screen; status as the list's band, no chip beside it, and a record's Status sentence never repeats its chip; every finished event on one list. Twice corrected: the independent check caught the first wording claiming one door while the strip still showed; the /design review then gave the strip a rule instead of leaving it to the frame
3A row that opens without a chevronA chevron closes every row that opensList and Past rows end in theirs; How it finished rows open nothing and carry none
4Status colour in a row's wordsColour on a chip, or a figure that is bad newsNone in rows; "still owed" amber only when money is owed
5Columns without a heading rowA table has its heading row; a row list has no data columnsThe desk Tournaments list and Past tournaments are tables with headings; the phones are row lists
6Two filter shapesOne filter shapeNo filter drawn: bands carry the grouping. A search or filter, when a club has many events, is Stage 2's toolbar (one line) — not needed at three events
7A right chevron on a row that expandsRight opens a placeEvery chevron opens a place (a record or a page)
8Sizes off the ladderThe type ladder: 10 · 11 · 12 · 14 · 16 · 20 · 24 · 32Titles 20, section headings 16, rows 14, captions 12, figures 24, chips 10. The printed page keeps the same steps at print size
9The eyebrowAn eyebrow is a trail or nothing; no club name above a title (1 Oct)Past tournaments' "UAT TEST ORG" and the list's "Organization" go
10A part with its own radiusA part keeps its family'sCards and frames 8px, the record the kit's window
11Two band shapesOne band: the label, then its count"Live 2", "Completed 1", "Archived 1"; "Sealed records" without a count when it holds a line
12Desk control heights34px on a computer (3 Oct); 44 on a phoneDesk buttons 34, the desk windows' too (drawn at 44 until the re-check after the /design review); phone buttons and icons 44, wide as well as tall
13A door drawn as a record rowA door to another place is the door cardSummary's door on the board is the door card
14The date formThe product's form"Oct 2–4, 2026", "Sun, Oct 4" (Stage 1's short weekday form); today's legacy Summary printed "2026-10-02 to 2026-10-04" (the kit page drops it)
15A chip's size10px, uppercase monoCompleted, Archived, Tournament Plus
16Phone lists as separate cardsA list whose rows fit is one frame (S.7)The list (today 222px cards of labelled lines) and Past tournaments are one frame with bands
§3.6—A row that opens, opens from anywhere; delete never a row actionList and Past rows; Delete ends the record
§3.7—Nothing to list: one sentence, no heading row over an empty bodySealed records: one sentence (Plus) or one lock line (Tournament plan)
§3.10.7—One lead markHow it finished: a trophy for a champion, a standings mark for a division without a final, never both
§3.10.8—A row that opens a form opens it full screen on a phoneThe event's record; the reuse step (shared, Stage 5: its own choice in D2)
K-08—Nothing conditional beside a table's chevronNamed: Reuse setup appears in Past tournaments' Completed band only, as Teams' Accept (A13, ruled) — the band is the condition
One lime—One main action per screen (A12)Board: Reuse this setup (Tournament plan: none). Summary: none. Tournaments: New tournament. Reuse step: Create the draft. Row actions olive
Buttons—An action is the portal's white button; a window-opening action an outlined button; a door olive text or a door card (1 Oct)Copy, Print, Archive, Reopen, Seal, Bring back: white (on a phone, Copy is the boxed 44px icon in every place — the /design review caught a bare olive glyph, a door's look, on the board). Summary's door: the door card. Public ledger: a white button with its arrow. "Finished events are in Past tournaments": olive text, a door
Locks—One plain line, never a dashed box (30 Sep)Every Plus lock on this tab; today's dashed Sealed box goes
Records—Reads first, edits whole; names its neighbours (30 Sep, 1 Oct)The event's record: pencil in the head, Previous / Next at the foot, at both widths. Found by the independent check: the phone record was first drawn with no foot — fixed
Tinted panels—Retired to a white callout with a coloured edge (21 Sep)The wrap-up card, the champions band, the reuse step's option cards and warning panel
A record—A win–loss record takes a hyphen; a score keeps its dash (19 Aug)3-0-0 on the board, Summary and the printed page, one format (the standings' own W-L-T); the final's 5–4 keeps its dash. Fixed by the /design review (the first draft wrote 3–0 and 3–0–0)
A figure—A figure counts what it names"Teams" is the 8 that played, on the board, Summary, the print and the record. Fixed by the /design review: the first draft carried today's 9 registrations
A meta line—Facts once, never restating (29 Aug)A record's line says its dates once ("Oct 2–4, 2026 · 8 teams · 15 games"). Fixed by the /design review (the year was said twice)
Mark required—A plain asterisk in the label's ink (26 Aug)The reuse step's four fields
One spelling—One word everywhere a customer reads itOne name, Summary (the /design review): the title, door card, lock lines and print, for "Post-event summary", the strip's "event summary" and Plan & billing's "post-tournament summaries". Flagged for /marketing: those words; "Tournaments" vs "Manage Tournaments"; "Past tournaments" vs "Archives"; "Live" (list) vs "Active" (status help) for a running event; "Reuse setup" (row) vs "Reuse this setup" (board, Summary)

A second, independent reviewer then read the drawing and its rendered pictures against the same written rules. It found one departure (the phone record had no Previous / Next foot — fixed) and three rows of this table that said more than the pictures showed (Records, the Summary door count, the ladder — reworded). It confirmed the buttons (door, action, a row's worded action), every lock as a plain line, the required asterisk in the label's ink, the 34px desk and 44px phone heights, no tinted rows, and the Exhibition's standings link. Not checked, and why: contrast is not measured on a drawing (the build measures it in both themes); the words are placeholders until /marketing.

The /design review (5 October), thirteen changes, all applied on your "go ahead": (1) "Teams" counts the 8 that played, not the 9 registered; (2) one name, Summary; (3) the strip above the phone bar gives way on the board and is never offered without Summary; (4) Copy on a phone is the boxed icon, an action; (5) each event lives in one list — the Tournaments list holds what's ahead, Past tournaments every finished event (A22 sharpened); (6) records with a hyphen, one format; (7) the print's columns true for every row; (8) a record's line says the year once; (9) Status opens with the day it finished, never repeating its chip (no archive date is stored, so none is drawn); (10) a full plan names the event holding the slot; (11) the confirm says "Move back to draft"; (12) the free board's Summary lock in the door card's place; (13) the door says the link is to share and the page is for your records. And one more, found re-checking the pictures: the desk record and its confirm drew their buttons at a phone's 44px; on a computer they are 34 (3 October), now drawn so.

D7 · One Tournaments list: every event on one page, and one door to it

Asked by the owner on 6 October, walking §276 step 1 (“where is Tournaments?”): “why don’t we just make one Tournaments and put past tournaments under active tournaments on the list of tournaments? do we need 2 nav buttons?” We don’t. The two lists were ruled for a scope reason (one page “changes the rail, which this stage doesn’t draw”, ask A22’s tradeoff). The /design review’s point was that no event sits on both lists, and one list keeps that, because each event still sits in exactly one band. Built, the split costs three things. The list has no door from inside an event (F48, the question that started this). On the one-slot plan, the event holding the slot is on the other page the morning after (F57). And Mark complete sends an event to another page. After: one page, “Tournaments”, with what’s ahead on top and what’s finished below it (Active · Draft · Completed · Archived · Sealed records), and one door, “Tournaments”, in Past tournaments’ place inside the Admin group, at a desk and on a phone (ruled D7a; the first drawing put it at the top of the rail and of More).

Stage 6 · The volunteers · phone only (a scoring-table tablet measured too) · true size · open this tab on your phone · drawn 7 October 2026 · ruled 7 October: V1–V7 as drawn, A25–A32 as recommended · built 7 October — the “Built” part

The scorekeeper and the gate keep their shape; what gets in a volunteer's way goes

A parent handed a phone at the scoring table or the gate does one job, fast. June's walk called these the strongest screens in the tournament product, and the measuring agrees: from the link to a submitted score is 3 taps and the typing, checking a team in is 1 tap, and switching between the two jobs is 1 tap. So this stage keeps every shape you ruled (the cards, the buckets under the thumb and the jobs as tabs, 7 August) and draws only what the measuring found in the way: an install banner that sits on the buckets and over an open score sheet, bars the page shows through, controls under 44px, a waiting count nobody can see, a gate volunteer who lands on the scorekeeper, the organizer's Staff kit printing the whole admin, and the gate's team sheet off the sheet rules.

Before is today's screen, captured on 7 October with the volunteer accounts on the Plus and free test clubs (read-only: every write was refused and recorded). The Plus event's games are in June, so the scorekeeper is shown on June 14, its busiest day. After is drawn in Warm only: both volunteer screens ignore the Warm/Dark setting by design (the shell pins the warm palette, because a gate phone is shared and a light screen reads in the sun — ruling R3, confirmed in code and on a phone set to Dark), so a Dark copy would draw a screen that cannot exist. The Staff kit is an organizer's page and follows the theme, so it has one. Every red flag, green chip and NEW / RESTYLED / UNCHANGED tag opens its note; the striped square beside each phone is 44px.

What the measuring found that F36 and June missed

  • The bars are see-through. The buckets and the tabs wear the portal bar's 92–97% ground without its blur, so a team name shows through under the thumb.
  • "11:30 A.M." — the game line and the gate's arrival chip draw the clock in capitals by style, which the spelling gate cannot see.
  • A volunteer invited for the gate lands on the scorekeeper, on accepting and on every later sign-in, though the invite promises the gate.
  • A score sent back returns silently, its numbers gone; a forfeit sits in no bucket but All.
  • The after-submit notice talks to the organizer and never leaves: "An admin can now review and finalize this result from Results & Scoring" (the page is called Results).
  • The Staff kit fails the formatting check (F14 said it works — it does, but its one-pager prints the admin).

The Exhibition: nothing a volunteer sees changes. Neither shell reads the format: the scorekeeper lists the day's games, the gate the accepted teams. Not drawn. The gate's board (the bucket bar inline, the owe line, the rows, the division picker) is Stage 1's and is drawn UNCHANGED; only what the shell adds around it is new or restyled.

V5 · Where each volunteer lands: the link works; the invite and the next morning forget the job

Walked for an official on both test clubs and read from code for staff (no test club has a staff member; nothing was added). The link or QR code always lands right: the sign-in returns to the address it was given, the scorekeeper's or the gate's. What goes wrong is everything without a link. The invite asks what a volunteer is "Helping with" (Both · Scorekeeping · Gate / check-in) and promises the gate volunteer "Opens the gate board" — but a new volunteer's accept, every later sign-in, the installed app and a guessed admin address all land on the scorekeeper, because the choice is used once, for an existing account's email, and kept nowhere. And staff: a bare sign-in lands on the organizer's game-day board — which is right for what staff is (it updates the schedule, posts announcements, scores and checks in, by default), and wrong only for a gate parent who was given the wrong role, which the invite makes easy (Staff is its default).

V7 · Your ruling · the Staff kit ruled 7 Oct · as drawn

The asks: all ruled 7 October, as recommended

Your paste-back of 7 October ruled every one as recommended, and V1–V7 as drawn; the boxes stay so the paste-back still reads them. Each has options, a recommendation and the tradeoff, and is a row on the Decisions tab. A25 is the prompt's first question, answered with a different recommendation than it proposed — because the code says staff isn't the gate parent's role (below). A26, A30, A31 and A32 are what the measuring found.

A25 · Where a staff member lands (J8-021) shared · Club Tier roles ruled 7 Oct

Tradeoff: the capability rule is sound but, on today's defaults, changes nothing: a staff member always holds the schedule and posts, so it fires only when an organizer has narrowed one by hand — and then the right role was a volunteer. Sending all staff to the gate takes the people who run rain delays away from the schedule. Shared: staff is a role on every plan, Club included, and its defaults were ruled in Club Tier Stage 1.

A26 · A volunteer lands on the job they were given (F62, found) shared · Club Tier roles ruled 7 Oct

Tradeoff: with the first, a gate volunteer who later needs to score must have their access changed in Members — a real permission, where today the choice is decoration. The second keeps both jobs open but adds data the roles' owners must carry. The third costs every gate volunteer one tap at every sign-in, and is honest.

A27 · The 44px floor on both shells (F36, F60) ruled 7 Oct

Tradeoff: about 2px taller per row of controls on a phone (the list's first game moves by nothing measurable — the eyebrow's removal pays for it); on a tablet the header grows to hold 44px doors within its 52px.

A28 · The Review bucket's waiting count (F36) ruled 7 Oct

Tradeoff: amber says "waiting", and here the waiting is the organizer's — but a volunteer can still correct a waiting score (Save correction), and the pill is the same mark the organizer sees for the same scores. Tinting the bucket is a tinted panel (retired) and says the status twice.

A29 · The gate's team sheet on the frame — it is the organizer's Check-in sheet too shared · the organizer's Check-in ruled 7 Oct

Tradeoff: the sheet is one component (F13: one board, two shells), and it also serves the schedule's reschedule sheet and two public follow sheets, which take the corners and dim with it. "Gate only" would fork the one board Stage 1 kept whole.

A30 · The shells' own sheets: the score sheet and the Account sheet (found: both are off the Sheet Frame) ruled 7 Oct

Tradeoff: a × beside Cancel is a second way to do one thing (why it was removed in August); without it, a volunteer on an iPhone home-screen app has Cancel only (no Back, no Escape) — which is in the thumb's reach at 44px. The Account sheet today covers the tabs it was opened from.

A31 · The install banner on the volunteer screens (F58, found) ruled 7 Oct

Tradeoff: above the bars it costs 91px until dismissed (screen one shows 2 whole games instead of 3); for a volunteer working the whole weekend, installing is worth it (the app opens on their job). The second option is defensible — a borrowed gate phone rarely wants an app — but the banner is the only place most people learn the app exists. The third leaves the buckets covered.

A32 · What a volunteer sees when a score is finalized or sent back (F63, found) ruled 7 Oct

Tradeoff: a volunteer who closed the app misses the notice and simply sees a game to score again — which is the true state. Storing it says more but adds a column for a rare event. Also in this ask, as build work: a finalized forfeit arriving live keeps "Pending Review" until a refresh, and a forfeit sits in no bucket but All.

The formatting check, run before you saw it

Stage 1's sixteen departures (plan §11), the table standard's §3.5–3.7 and §3.10, and every ruling since — including the four newest (a filter is quiet until it filters; the olive pill chooses what is read; a close × is a plain glyph, 7 October; a row's flags under the name on a phone, 6 October). The volunteer screens are their own ruled exception to the nav grammar (the inert wordmark, the bars under the thumb), so a row below says where the shells keep their own rule and why.

#The checkThe ruleThis drawing
1A screen without its title bandEvery screen keeps its title bandField scores, Check-in, Staff kit: 20px title face, icon actions on the line. Today the scorekeeper's title is 27px (off the ladder) under a "SCOREKEEPER" eyebrow
2A fact said more than onceA status is said onceThe waiting count is the pill on the count, not a second number; the after-submit sentence once, in a fading notice; a team's arrival once per surface — on the row, the IN chip with the time beside it; in the team's sheet, which covers the row, its context line ("In · 8:59 a.m."). Today the sheet says it twice (its eyebrow and a "CHECKED IN" chip); the chip goes. Sharpened by the second reviewer, who counted the row and the sheet as one surface
3A row that opens without a chevronA chevron closes every row that opensThe gate's rows (Stage 1's, kept). Named, kept: the scorekeeper's game card is a whole-card button with no chevron (ADC specimen 7, the volunteer's register: a card, not a list row)
4Status colour in a row's wordsColour on a chip, or a figure that is bad news"Owes $475" amber (money owed), everything else plain; the arrival time leaves the green chip
5Columns without a heading rowA table has its heading rowNo table on these phone screens; the gate's desk table is Stage 1's (Team · Roster · Payment)
6Two filter shapesOne filter shape; quiet until it filters (7 Oct)The buckets are a bar of four single-choice buttons, the chosen one olive (the gate's bar, 29 Sep) — the same on both shells. The scorekeeper's Filters fold keeps its count badge, plain at rest
7A right chevron on a row that expandsRight opens a placeEvery chevron opens the team's sheet
8Sizes off the ladder10 · 11 · 12 · 14 · 16 · 20 · 24 · 32Titles 20 (today 27 on the scorekeeper); sheet heads and menu rows 16; rows, callouts and the tablet's header doors 14; captions 12; the shell's club line and small-capitals labels 11; chips 10; the score numeral 38 (a field's figure, kept from today's 37.6 — the one named size off the ladder). Found by the second reviewer: the first draft carried today's sizes over in five places (the callouts and the tablet doors at 13, the Account rows at 15, two labels at 10.5); now on the ladder
9The eyebrowAn eyebrow is a trail or nothing; no club name above a title"SCOREKEEPER" over "Field scores" goes; "ENTER SCORE" becomes a sentence head; the club's name lives in the shell's header only (as today)
10A part with its own radiusA part keeps its family'sCards 8px; every sheet 18px at the top (D4, the frame); today the score sheet is an 8px floating card and the team sheet 12px

12Control heights34 on a computer, 44 on a phoneEverything a volunteer taps is 44, on a phone and on a tablet (A27); the Staff kit at a desk 34
13A door drawn as a record rowA door to another place is a door card or olive textThe Staff kit's Open and "Invite a volunteer" are olive text with their arrows; Copy link and Print are actions (white)
14The date and the clockThe product's form; "8:00 a.m.", lowercase, everywhere a customer reads a time (26 Aug)"11:30 a.m." and "8:59 a.m." out of every capitals style (F61); the day field is the phone's own control (kept)
15A chip's size10px, uppercase monoUp next, Needs a score, IN — no time inside a chip
16Phone lists as separate cardsA list whose rows fit is one frame (S.7)The gate is one frame (Stage 1). Named, kept: the scorekeeper's games stay cards with gaps — each is a 160px whole-card button with two names stacked, the field-grade target June praised; one frame of 160px rows would change nothing but the gaps. Yours to overrule
Sheets—Two layers by one test; three heads; × a plain glyph (5 & 7 Oct)Score sheet = form, sentence head, Cancel the way out (A30's named exception); Account = menu over the bar, label, no ×; the team sheet = record head + 44px plain ×. Every sheet carries the frame's grab line (found by the second reviewer: the first draft drew the score sheet without it)
Waiting—A waiting count is the amber pill (1 Oct)Review's count, phone and tablet

Buttons—An action is the white button; a door is olive text (1 Oct)Today, Filters, Cancel, Copy link, Mark paid, Add roster, Print: white. Open, Invite a volunteer, the header's "Check-in →": olive text. The Account sheet's two rows (Install this app, Sign out) are menu rows, one treatment in ink (fixed after the second reviewer: the first draft drew Sign out olive, Install in ink)
Tinted panels—Retired to a white callout with a coloured edge (21 Sep)The policy note (an amber edge where the organizer reviews, olive where scores are final at once — both drawn), the finished-event line, Add roster's panel. Mark paid's amber box becomes the white button (the Buttons row)
Bars—A pinned bar over the page is opaque or blurredBoth bars opaque (today 92–97% with no blur, F59)
Fixed Warm—R3: the volunteer shells are warm whatever the phone saysDrawn Warm only; no Dark copy (the screen cannot be dark). The Staff kit, an admin page, has its Dark copy
The shells' own rules—The top-nav audit's ruled exception (an inert wordmark; doors in the tab bar on a phone, in the header above 640px); Option C (7 Aug)Kept as ruled, drawn unchanged except sizes and grounds
One spelling—One word everywhere a customer reads itFlagged for /marketing: "Submit for Review" / "Finalize Score" / "Save Correction" (Title Case); "Enter Score"; the review note's "admin review"; "Results & Scoring" (now Results); "Staff Kit" (tab) vs "Staff kit"; "Settings & Access" vs the rail's "Settings & access"; the role "Scorekeeper" for a gate volunteer; "Un-pay"

A second, independent reviewer then read the drawing and its rendered pictures against the same written rules. It found eight departures, all fixed: type off the ladder in five places; the Account sheet's contents tagged Unchanged when their shape changes; its two rows in two treatments; the tablet drawn as a header strip only (now the whole top at 768); the olive "final at once" note claimed and not drawn (now drawn); the banner's icon reading as a bug (it is the app's real icon, an F over an L — now the icon itself); the team sheet's 44px × not stated (now stated and measured); the score sheet without the grab line every sheet carries (added). And four claims that said more than the pictures: "the list drops 208px" was read off a 2× picture — the notice is 88px and the list drops about 104 (corrected here, in F64 and in the plan); "the list stays put" (it moves up a card: "doesn't drop"); Mark paid listed under tinted panels (it is a button); and a team's arrival said "once" (once per surface, now said so). It confirmed the gate's six whole rows and its 237 vs 226, every clock in lowercase, the chips, the eyebrow's removal, the amber pill only above zero, the doors and actions, one lime per screen, opaque bars, and every figure on the tab against the pictures. Two points stand as drawn, with the reason: the 768 "before" picture is clean (the tab bar it saw came from a screenshot of this hub, not the capture), and the after-submit notice is the product's toast, the dark pill every stage has drawn.

Not checked, and why: contrast is not measured on a drawing (the build measures it); the words are placeholders until /marketing; the QR squares are stand-ins.

Not drawn: the build's work

  • Any change to a landing or a role's capabilities (A25, A26) — shared: the roles and the Members invite are Club Tier's, the landing resolver is the platform's. Drawn here as the ask; built by its owners, or by this stage only on their word.
  • The banner's position contract: the volunteer shells publish their bottom height for it, and the install-banner guard test (which today names the shells' sheets as not covered) gains them. The banner is the whole product's; its warm look on the shells is a variant, not a fork.
  • A clock in capitals (F61): a time never sits inside a capitals style; the spelling gate cannot see a style, so the build checks the rendered words.
  • The live update's forfeit (F63): a finalized forfeit arriving live keeps "Pending Review" until a refresh; a forfeit counts in no bucket but All.
  • The old look's retirement in every file Stage 6 rebuilds: the scorekeeper page and its sheet (scorekeeper.module.css, 58 kit-scoped rules), the shells' shared sheet (DayOfShell.module.css, 25), the gate page's sheet (6), the sign-out button's inline patch and the day-of-kit patches file, the Staff kit's sheet (10 — no stage named it until now), and the admin bottom sheet's old layer if A29 moves it. Held by npm run check:old-look and the strict admin colour gate.
  • The build prompt (written 7 October, after your rulings): TOURNAMENT_ADMIN_REDESIGN_STAGE6_BUILD_PROMPT.md. It asks you two placements the drawing does not show at its start — P1 who may change a volunteer’s jobs after the invite (today only an owner changes a member’s access; recommended: whoever may invite may switch a volunteer’s two jobs, and nothing else) and P2 a volunteer with neither job (recommended: Members refuses switching off the last one) — and its definition of done includes the old-look retirement above. Writing it re-read the code A26 rests on: it holds with no new data. It also found the shared team sheet has five users, not four (Teams’ phone view settings too).
